description: Both sulfate and ginger need to be added to a shampoo. One unit of sulfate takes 0.5 minutes to be effective while one unit of ginger takes 0.75 minutes to be effective. The shampoo must contain at least 100 units of sulfates and a total of 400 units of both ingredient. Since too much sulfate can damage the hair, there can be at most twice the amount of sulfate as ginger in the shampoo. How many units of each should be added to the shampoo to minimize the total amount of time it takes for the mixture to be effective? (Note: one must be added before the other)

TimePerUnitSulfate.definition: Time taken for one unit of sulfate to be effective

TimePerUnitGinger.definition: Time taken for one unit of ginger to be effective

TotalUnits.definition: Total units of sulfate and ginger

MaxSulfateToGingerRatio.definition: Maximum allowed ratio of sulfate to ginger

objective.description: Minimize the total time required for the shampoo mixture to become effective

constraints.description: The number of sulfate units must be greater than or equal to the minimum required sulfate units
The total number of sulfate and ginger units must equal the specified total units
The number of sulfate units must be less than or equal to the maximum allowed sulfate-to-ginger ratio multiplied by the number of ginger units
